@@ -96,5 +96,5 @@
 - Priority inheritance: prerequisite epic inherits the highest priority of all HLRs it transitively enables
 - An epic blocking all P0 work is implicitly P0
-- Priority split: when an epic maps to HLRs at multiple priority levels, check whether the lower-priority HLRs represent distinct, deferrable features. A feature is "distinct and deferrable" only when it could ship as its own epic with independent user value AND does not share data structures, UI surfaces, or API endpoints with the P0 work. If yes, split them into separate epics by priority so each can be planned independently. If the lower-priority HLR is incidental to the P0 work (error handling, doc coverage, config override that falls out of the same implementation) or is tightly coupled to the same implementation surface, keep it bundled — splitting tightly coupled work creates duplication and artificial boundaries.
+- Priority split: when an epic maps to HLRs at multiple priority levels, check whether the lower-priority HLRs represent distinct, deferrable features. A feature is "distinct and deferrable" only when it could ship as its own epic with independent user value AND does not share data structures, UI surfaces, or API endpoints with the P0 work. If yes, split them into separate epics by priority so each can be planned independently. If the lower-priority HLR is incidental to the P0 work (error handling, doc coverage, config override that falls out of the same implementation) or is tightly coupled to the same implementation surface, keep it bundled — splitting tightly coupled work creates duplication and artificial boundaries. **When you keep a lower-priority HLR bundled, record the priority-split analysis inline in the summary's HLR Traceability Matrix row (Step 8a):** flag the row as `bundled` and state in the row why the HLR is not a separately schedulable deliverable — it edits the same call sites, data structure, or surface as the higher-priority work, so splitting would double-touch the same files or create two epics building the same surface. With that flag, the priority label on the bundled HLR reads as relative value, not a deferral signal. A bundling rationale that lives only in a separate prose section or a footnote after the matrix reads to a reviewer as an unanalyzed priority collapse — the analysis must be visible in the matrix row itself.
 - **Redundant / overlapping HLRs — consolidate, never split:** strategies merged from multiple sources sometimes state one capability twice in different words (e.g. "select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side" and "a diff view highlighting which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs" — the diff view is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run data). When two HLRs describe the same data structure, UI surface, or API endpoint for the same component and team — one a restatement or presentation mode of the other — they are ONE capability: cover both with a single epic whose HLR Traceability lists both HLR ids, at the higher of the two priorities. Do not split them into separate epics by priority label: on a shared surface a P0/P1 pair is redundant wording, not a deferral signal, and splitting produces two epics building the same surface plus an artificial serialization edge between them — a boundary violation even when the second epic only extends the first's surface.
 - `docs-authoring` priority exception: `docs-authoring` epics are exempt from priority inheritance. They do not push their priority upstream to the implementations they depend on. Instead, derive their priority from the strategy frontmatter `priority` field: Critical→P0, Major→P1, Normal/Minor/Undefined→P2. If the field is missing or empty, default to P2.

+   - **Health Warnings** (priority inversions, scope traps — if any). When the strategy's effort estimate or your scope arithmetic puts an epic above ~2 weeks (one sprint) of work and you keep it as ONE logical change — a single mechanical pass over one surface, one audit, where a split would duplicate the audit or fragment the change — do not leave the overage as a bare note: record a **re-split trigger**, the concrete planning condition under which the epic should be re-split (e.g. "re-split if the call-site audit exceeds the estimated volume", "split the logistics work out if the campaign outgrows a sprint of effort"). A justified overage with a recorded trigger is a managed trade-off; a bare "above guideline" note is an unresolved defect that every later review will re-dock.
    - **Tiered Delivery** (if applicable — Tier 1 vs Tier 2 split)

Do not flag priority collapse on a triaged strategy — all HLRs are bundled intentionally.
